nodes.title: Limit reusable project-source search to prevent unbounded tree/DB loads

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reserve cap slots for the actual search hit**

When `sourcesByKey` already has 49 entries, a node hit from a new project adds the project ancestor first, taking the map to the 50-result cap, and the estimate/tab/node additions that follow are dropped by this guard. In the component-library UI the ancestor can fail the active query filter while the actual matching node is absent, so users see no result for a valid hit. Treat the hit plus its ancestors as a bundle, or add/reserve the matching source before filling the last slot with ancestors.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not cap away the node that matched the prefilter**

This bounded tree load only materializes the first 200 sorted nodes per tab after the DB prefilter has already selected an estimate because some group/area name matched. In a large estimate where the matching node sorts after that prefix, `collectProjectNodeSearchSources` searches a truncated tree and silently omits the real match, often returning no visible result for the query. The prefilter needs to carry matched node IDs/details through, or the materialization must include those matched nodes rather than an arbitrary prefix.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply estimate cap before fetching sheets**

This limit is applied only after every selected project's sheets have already been fetched: `listProjectEstimateSheets()` delegates to `listProjectEstimateSheetsForProject`, which runs an unbounded `select(...).eq(project_id).order(...)`. An authenticated user with a project containing thousands of estimates can still force those rows to be loaded on each two-character search, so the availability fix does not actually bound the estimate-list DB work; use a search-specific bounded query or pass the limit into the repository call.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Deduplicate estimates before applying the row cap**

This prefilter limits raw matching node rows rather than distinct `estimate_id`s, so one large estimate with 100 matching groups/areas can consume the entire result window and prevent other matching estimates from ever being materialized. In that case searches for terms shared across estimates return only the crowded estimate even though the materialization cap is supposed to allow up to 10 estimates; make the prefilter distinct/grouped by estimate or otherwise cap per estimate.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bound project retrieval before slicing**

The new project cap is applied only after `listCurrentWorkspaceProjects()` has already loaded the full project list and related project metadata, so workspaces with many readable projects can still force that unbounded DB/read path on every search before this slice discards most rows. To make the availability fix effective for project scale, use a search-specific bounded project query or push the limit into the repository call instead of slicing the fully materialized result.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Limit the tab fan-out before loading trees**

Even with per-tree node/row caps, a matched estimate with many active tabs still fans out into one `getEstimateTabTree` call per tab via this `tabs.map`, so a single matching estimate can trigger hundreds of bounded tree queries in parallel. Since users can create/duplicate tabs and there is no tab cap in this search path, cap the tab list or materialize only tabs that matched the prefilter/display search before loading trees.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep legacy-schema search from selecting estimate_tab_id**

When the tab migration has not been applied, this unguarded node prefilter now selects `estimate_tab_id` and immediately throws `matchingNodeError` before any legacy fallback can run. The surrounding reusable-source paths still opt into legacy `estimate_tabs`/`estimate_tab_id` fallback, and the previous prefilter selected only `estimate_id`, so any 2+ character project-source search regresses to a server error on those supported legacy schemas.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve punctuation for exact name searches**

When a user searches for an exact stored name containing punctuation, the query is rewritten but the candidate text and ILIKE target are not normalized the same way; for example `Smith, LLC` becomes `smith llc`, which no longer matches a project, estimate, tab, or node named `Smith, LLC`. This regresses exact searches that previously used only trimmed/lower-cased input, so either keep the raw pattern or normalize both sides consistently.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore archived tabs when pinning node search tabs**

When the one-row node prefilter happens to return a matching node from an archived tab, this records that archived `estimate_tab_id` as the only tab to materialize for the estimate. `getEstimateTabs()` only returns non-archived tabs, so `tabsToMaterialize` becomes empty; if the same estimate also has an active matching node, the arbitrary `limit(1)` row can hide a valid result that the previous all-active-tabs materialization would have found.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Batch the node prefilter instead of looping per estimate**

When a search has no node matches, or the matches are in later estimates, this loop now issues one `estimate_nodes` query per accessible estimate, up to the 100-estimate cap, before it can return or continue to tab-name matching. That turns every debounced search into as many as 100 serial DB round trips even though the previous prefilter used a single `in("estimate_id", accessibleEstimateIds)` query; use one bounded batched query (then dedupe/group client-side) to keep the availability fix from trading unbounded tree loads for request fan-out.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Attach legacy prefilter hits to the synthetic tab**

When running against the supported legacy schema where `estimate_tab_id` is missing, the new retry succeeds but stores prefiltered node hits with `tabId: null`; if that matched node sorts beyond the 200-node legacy tree limit, this guard prevents the fallback source from ever being emitted because the only materialized tab is the synthetic `legacy-main`. Fresh evidence after the retry fix is that legacy rows now reach this fallback path with no tab id, so searches can still return no result for a real matched legacy node unless null-tab hits are associated with the synthetic tab.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Search both raw and normalized node/tab patterns**

When the user types punctuation that the stored node or tab name does not contain, this raw ILIKE prefilter prevents the estimate from ever being materialized even though the in-memory matcher now strips punctuation. For example, `Smith, LLC` normalizes to `smith llc` and would match a node named `Smith LLC`, but the DB prefilter now sends `%Smith, LLC%`; the previous normalized prefilter would have found that row. Consider querying both the raw and normalized patterns, or otherwise applying the same normalization before the prefilter.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
Fixed in 31222606. Node and tab prefilters now run raw and normalized search patterns, so punctuation-normalized values like Smith LLC are found by a Smith, LLC query.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Order shared projects before applying the project limit**

For users with more than 20 shared projects and few/no owned projects, this slices `project_members`/`estimate_sheet_members` IDs before fetching and ordering the actual project rows. Those membership queries are unordered here, so project-source search can ignore a recently updated or matching shared project solely because its membership row was after the arbitrary first 20; apply the limit after ordering shared projects by project metadata, or use a bounded ordered shared-project query.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
Fixed in 31222606. Shared project IDs are fetched and ordered as project rows before the final project list limit is applied.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Filter estimates by the query before applying the cap**

When a project has more than 100 estimates, or an earlier project consumes the workspace-wide 100 slots, this fetches only the first sheet-code-ordered prefix before running estimate-name checks and node/tab prefilters. A matching estimate outside that arbitrary prefix is never placed in `accessibleEstimateIds`, so searches for its estimate name, sheet code, tab, or node now return nothing even though the previous path considered it; make the bounded estimate read search-aware before applying the cap.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 31222606 and hardened in add6a38b. Estimate search now applies raw/normalized query matching before returning capped candidates, with a post-dedupe limit so merged query branches stay bounded.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Normalize the client filter for server search hits**

This server matcher now returns punctuation-normalized hits such as project `Smith, LLC` for query `Smith LLC`, but the component-library tree filters the merged result set again with raw lower-case substring matching in `projectSourceMatchesQuery`. In that UI path the server hit is immediately removed, so normalized project/estimate/tab matches can still show no result unless the client uses the same normalization or skips re-filtering server search hits.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
Fixed in 31222606. Client-side project-source filtering now uses the same normalized reusable-source matcher as server search.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Search projects before applying the project cap**

This search path now loads only the first 20 workspace projects and then checks project names in memory, so a workspace with more than 20 accessible projects cannot find an older project by its exact name if it falls outside that updated-at prefix. The previous implementation considered all accessible projects; use a query-aware bounded project lookup or include name-matched projects before truncating the candidate set.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
Fixed in 31222606. Search includes query-aware project-name reads before the project cap and merges those with recent candidates.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use a lightweight project lookup for search**

For users with many favorites, shared memberships, or invitations, this new two-branch search path now runs the full `listCurrentWorkspaceProjects` repository flow twice for each debounced query; fresh evidence after the limit option is that the helper still performs unbounded reads of `project_favorites`, `estimate_favorites`, `project_members`, `estimate_sheet_members`, plus publication/invite metadata that this search only needs for readable project ids/names. This keeps the hot reusable-source search path unbounded outside the projects table and doubles work that the previous single call did, so use a search-specific lightweight access query or add a mode that skips unrelated workspace metadata.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 58ed15cd. Reusable-source search now uses listCurrentWorkspaceProjectSearchCandidates, which reads only bounded project ids/names plus shared membership ids instead of the full workspace project metadata flow.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply project search to shared projects**

When `options.search` is set, this `ilike` is only applied to the owned workspace-project query; the shared-project query below still fetches all shared ids and then the final `projectItems` cap slices by updated_at. For a user with more than 20 shared projects, an older shared project whose name exactly matches the search can be absent from `matchingProjectResult`, so reusable-source search never examines its estimates/tabs/nodes. Apply the same search predicate before capping shared projects, or merge name-matched shared projects ahead of the generic shared-project prefix.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 58ed15cd. Shared-project reads now apply the same raw/normalized project-name search predicates before ordering and capping, both in the lightweight search-candidate API and the full project-list search path.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve sheet-code hits when capping estimate search**

When a project has 100 estimate-name matches for a query such as `01`, an estimate whose `sheet_code` exactly equals `01` but whose name does not match can be appended by the sheet-code branch after the first 100 name rows and then discarded by this post-merge slice. `searchReusableProjectSources` only prefilters the returned estimate IDs, so that exact sheet-code search returns no estimate/tab/node hit for the omitted sheet.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply the query length cap to the raw search branch**

For inputs longer than 120 characters, `query` is capped but `rawQuery` is not, and the raw value is passed into the project/estimate candidate reads and raw ILIKE prefilter pattern. An authenticated caller can therefore submit a very large search string and still force oversized PostgREST filters/URLs despite the new `REUSABLE_PROJECT_SOURCE_SEARCH_MAX_QUERY_LENGTH`; cap `rawQuery` before using it for any DB-backed search branch.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Batch estimate candidate reads before prefiltering**

When a search has many candidate projects and few/no estimate-name matches, this await runs inside the project loop and the recent-estimates branch immediately below runs afterward, so one debounced query can spend up to two serial `listProjectEstimateSheets` DB round trips per project before it can even prefilter nodes/tabs or return. Keep the global caps, but batch the estimate candidate read across project IDs or use bounded parallelism so the availability fix does not turn 50 project candidates into ~100 serial repository calls.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

nodes.title: fix: reconcile partial template batch inserts

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reconcile partial failures after newer optimistic edits**

When a batched template drop partially fails and the user makes another tree-changing optimistic edit before the server action resolves, the revision guard just above this branch skips applying `result.tree`. This new partial-failure path then only logs/toasts, so the failed templates that were added optimistically remain visible even though they were never committed; this preserves the same UI/DB divergence the change is trying to fix. Please make the partial-failure case trigger a safe reconciliation/refetch or otherwise remove the failed optimistic nodes even when the revision has advanced.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove moved optimistic roots during reconciliation**

If the user drags one of the just-added template roots before a partial batch failure resolves, this reconciliation only scans the original target parent's immediate children, so the moved optimistic root is left in the tree while the server-committed roots are inserted. Fresh evidence for this remaining race is that template clones get UUID ids from `createEstimateRowItemId()`, so the tree's `startsWith("optimistic-")` drag guard does not block them; remove the `optimisticRootNodeIds` wherever they are in the current tree before inserting committed roots under the original parent.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Don't invalidate later optimistic insert reconciliation**

When another template/node insert is started after this batch drop but before the partial-failure response resolves, this unguarded `setEstimateTree` bumps the shared tree revision. The later insert's success handler still uses the revision guard pattern (`getEstimateTreeRevision() === nextRevision`), so its authoritative server tree is skipped and its optimistic UUID nodes can remain visible even though the server committed different ids; use a reconciliation path that does not make newer in-flight inserts miss their own server replacement, or force a refetch after the partial merge.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Protect partial reconciliation from later rollbacks**

When a user starts another optimistic mutation after the batch (for example adding a row) and this partial-failure reconciliation resolves before that later mutation fails, the tree changes here without advancing the revision. The later mutation's rollback still sees its expected revision and restores the `previousTree` it captured before this reconciliation, which still contains all of the batch's optimistic template roots, so failed templates can reappear and committed roots can disappear. This needs a revision/epoch or rollback strategy that prevents stale optimistic snapshots from undoing the partial reconciliation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
Fixed in 83c7d132. Partial batch reconciliation now advances the tree revision, and stale later failures remove only their own optimistic roots instead of restoring an older tree snapshot.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve existing committed-root positions**

If the current tree has already picked up one of these committed server ids before the partial-failure handler runs (for example from an intervening refetch, project-source insert, or another server tree apply), this helper removes that node from wherever it currently is and always appends the copy from `result.tree` to the original target parent. In that interleaving, a committed template that the user/server has already ordered relative to later siblings is moved to the end locally, leaving the sheet order divergent until a later full refresh. Reinsert only the still-optimistic placeholders, or preserve the current/server ordering for committed ids that are already present.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
Fixed in 83c7d132. The reconciliation helper now preserves committed roots already present in the current tree and appends only missing committed roots.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use the refreshed tree when no local edit intervened**

On a partial failure this branch always merges only the committed roots into the current cache, even when `getEstimateTreeRevision() === nextRevision` proves no local tree edit superseded the batch. If the server refresh includes any other authoritative change made while the batch was in flight, such as a collaborator adding or moving a sibling under the same parent, that change is ignored even though the action already returned `result.tree` and the toast says the sheet was refreshed. Apply the full refreshed tree in the non-superseded case and reserve the merge path for advanced revisions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
Fixed in 83c7d132. Partial success now applies the refreshed result.tree when no local edit intervened; the merge path is used only after the revision advances.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove optimistic descendants during reconciliation**

When a batch insert partially fails (or a failed batch is caught after another tree edit), this reconciler only removes children whose ids are in `optimisticRootNodeIds`. That set is built from the cloned top-level template nodes, while `cloneTemplateNodesForEstimate` gives every descendant its own UUID-like id and the tree drag guard only blocks ids starting with `optimistic-`. If the user drags an optimistic child/area out of the inserted template before the action settles, that child is no longer under a removed root and survives the reconciliation even though it was never committed. Track and remove all cloned template node ids, not just root ids.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
Fixed forward on main in 500c2dae. Reconciliation now tracks every optimistic cloned node id, so optimistic descendants moved outside the original root are removed wherever they landed.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve nodes moved into optimistic roots**

When a user drags an existing sheet node into a just-added template root before the partial-failure response settles, this removal drops the entire optimistic subtree, including that pre-existing node. That drag is allowed because cloned template roots get UUID-like ids rather than the `optimistic-` prefix the tree guard blocks, and the later reorder rollback is revision-guarded, so once this reconciliation bumps the revision the rollback can no longer restore the hidden node. Either block drops into pending template roots or preserve non-optimistic descendants when removing the failed placeholders.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
Fixed forward on main in 500c2dae. Removing a failed optimistic placeholder now hoists/preserves non-optimistic descendants, so existing nodes moved into a pending template root are not lost.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep partial commits visible if refresh fails**

After an earlier template RPC has committed, this partial-failure path breaks out and then relies on `refreshInsertedEstimateTree`; if that refresh/read throws or returns missing data, the action rejects and the client runs the full-failure rollback/removal path without the committed root ids. In that scenario the first template remains committed in Postgres but disappears from the sheet cache until a later reload, recreating the UI/DB divergence this change is meant to avoid. Return an explicit partial result or trigger a safe refetch/reconciliation even when the post-write refresh fails.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed forward on main in 500c2dae. After a partial commit, refresh failure now returns explicit partial evidence with refreshFailed instead of throwing into the full rollback path; the client keeps the optimistic committed view and triggers a refetch.

nodes.title: Bound reusable project-source search to prevent DB fan-out and add rate limits

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply the estimate cap after matching**

When a project has more than 25 estimates, this truncates the searchable allow-list before any matching happens. `listProjectEstimateSheetsForProject` orders by `sheet_code`, so an exact query for sheet 26 (or any tab/node inside it) is never checked by the in-memory estimate loop or the Supabase `estimate_id` filters, and the Templates search shows no reusable source until the user manually expands that project. Please cap returned/materialized matches instead of dropping searchable estimates up front.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Limit DB matches by distinct estimates**

When a broad search term matches more than 50 group/area rows in one estimate, this raw-row limit can fill `matchingNodeRows` with only that estimate id. Because only returned ids are added to `estimatesToMaterialize`, other estimates with matching nodes are silently omitted even when the 50-result cap still has room. Limit/group by distinct `estimate_id` before materializing, or fetch enough rows to cover distinct estimates.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Search all projects before applying the project cap**

When an account has more than 50 non-pending projects, this slices the project list before any estimate/tab/node matching. A query for an estimate or node in project 51 is excluded from `accessibleEstimateIds` and from both Supabase prefilters, so the Templates search can show no reusable source even though expanding that project manually would load it. Apply the cap to returned/materialized matches, or add pagination, instead of dropping projects from the candidate set.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Let the Terms acceptance action bypass the gate**

With the new default `enforceTermsAcceptance ?? true`, existing callers such as `acceptCurrentTermsAction` (`src/lib/legal/actions.ts:28`) now redirect unaccepted users back to `/workshop/terms` before `recordCurrentTermsAcceptance` can run. In the exact scenario this gate is for—a signed-in user who has not accepted the current Terms—the form submission cannot persist acceptance, so the user is stuck in the Terms gate until this action opts out like the page does.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Gate getCurrentUserContext-only protected endpoints too**

This new enforcement only runs for `requireCurrentUserContext`, but repo-wide search shows protected direct-call surfaces still use `getCurrentUserContext` without any Terms check, e.g. `src/app/api/projects/images/route.ts:181` serves private project images and `src/lib/collaboration/realtime-identity-actions.ts:49` issues realtime identity envelopes. A signed-in user who has not accepted the current Terms can still call those endpoints directly and bypass the legal gate this change is meant to apply to protected API/server-action flows, so either the direct callers need explicit checks or the shared helper boundary needs to cover them safely.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep Terms-check failures inside the export JSON error path**

If the new Terms acceptance lookup fails (for example the `legal_terms_acceptances` migration/grant/RLS is missing or Supabase returns an error), `getCurrentUserTermsAcceptanceStatus` throws here before the route enters its existing `try/catch`. That bypasses the export route's fetch-then-blob contract documented just below, so the client gets a framework 500/non-JSON response instead of the clean JSON error handling used for other DB/export failures; wrap this check in the same error path or return a controlled JSON 500.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Gate server actions that skip the auth helper**

Fresh evidence beyond the earlier direct-caller fix: this enforcement only runs for callers of `requireCurrentUserContext`, but some protected `use server` mutations still use `createSupabaseServerClient` directly and never hit this helper. For example, `src/lib/projects/actions.ts:279` (`updateProjectDetails`, wired from the project details forms) updates project metadata without calling `requireCurrentUserContext`, `getCurrentUserContext`, or `getCurrentUserTermsAcceptanceStatus`, so an authenticated user with a stale page/action id after a Terms version bump can still mutate project data before accepting the current Terms.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Return JSON failures for gated API routes**

When this default gate runs inside App Route Handlers that call `requireCurrentUserContext` (for example `POST /api/projects/images` and the component-library upload routes), `redirect()` produces an HTTP redirect to `/workshop/terms` instead of the JSON error those XHR/fetch clients expect. In the stale-open-page case after Terms are updated, the upload clients follow/parse the Terms page rather than receiving a controlled 403, leading to incomplete/null upload responses or generic client errors; API routes need an API-native Terms check or an option that does not redirect.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Gate the AI auth helper before provider/data access**

The new Terms enforcement still misses the protected AI API path because `/api/ai/ask` and `/api/ai/package-builder` authenticate through `getAiRequestUserContext` (`src/lib/ai/auth.ts:14`) rather than this helper, and that custom helper only checks the Supabase session/workspace. A signed-in user who has not accepted the current Terms can still call those endpoints directly; the ask route reads workspace context and the package-builder route can continue into its draft/apply flow before any Terms check runs.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Align the viewed snapshot with the RPC lock**

When a recipient posts from an old tab after a content-only republish, this now sends the session's viewed version (e.g. `1`) to `submitSharedLinkDecision`, but the repository still calls the existing `submit_client_response` RPC, whose migration rejects unless `p_expected_snapshot_version` equals the current `project_publications.snapshot_version` (`supabase/migrations/20260603210653_lock_shared_link_response_snapshot_version.sql:37`). After the publication is at version `2`, the RPC raises and the route returns 409, so the new stale-view flow is still broken in production; the same mismatch exists for comments via `insert_client_comment`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refresh legacy sessions instead of looping on reload**

For sessions minted before this cookie field existed (still valid for up to 24h), `verifySharedLinkSessionCookieValue` continues to accept the cookie because `snapshotVersion` is optional, but `readSharedLinkSessionCookieSnapshotVersion` returns `undefined` here and the route returns a 409 telling the recipient to reload. Reloading `/share/[token]` without the original `recipient` query only revalidates the same cookie and never reissues it with a snapshot, so these recipients stay unable to comment/decide until they delete cookies or reopen the original recipient link; the decision route has the same path.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the snapshot per rendered view, not per session**

This stores the viewed snapshot in the long-lived browser session cookie, but that cookie is shared by every tab and is not refreshed when `/share/[token]` later renders a newer snapshot without the `recipient` query. A recipient can therefore reload and view version 2 while still submitting the cookie's old version 1, or open the recipient link in a second tab and overwrite the cookie to version 2 while an old version-1 tab is still open; in both cases the mutation no longer carries the snapshot actually shown in the tab. The viewed version needs to be tied to the rendered page/request rather than frozen in the reusable session credential.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Closed after landing the fix directly on main in 20fd0296.

Evidence:

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Page through all recipients before invalidating tokens**

Those stale raw recipient tokens can still be paired with the newly rotated base `/share/<token>` because the publication row id is preserved, leaving exactly the large-recipient case that rotation is meant to revoke; use pagination or a server-side RPC/update that covers all rows.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make token rotation and recipient revocation atomic**

If this recipient read or any later per-recipient update fails after the publication row has already been updated, the action throws but the new base token is still persisted while any not-yet-updated recipient hashes remain valid. In that failure state, a refreshed manager view can expose the new `/share/<token>`, and old emailed recipient tokens for rows that were not invalidated still authenticate against the same publication id; move the base-token update and recipient revocation into one database transaction/RPC so rotation cannot partially commit.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guard rotation against concurrent recipient resends**

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reset recipient delivery state after rotating credentials**

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Shorten the Unix-socket directory**

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid sequential sibling sort updates**

When dragging an existing template node before/after a sibling, this loop writes the new `sort_order` values one row at a time. Since the template editor drag/drop path calls this action, users cannot reliably reorder template structure nodes.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disable area-node inserts at the template root**

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Rebase optimistic reorder on latest cached area tree**

`nextNodes` is derived from `localNodes`, which is initialized from server props and not kept in sync with row-level cache edits (e.g. insert/replace/delete operations in `EstimateSheetContent` that update `estimateQueryKeys.areaTree`). Writing `nextNodes` directly into the query cache here can therefore overwrite newer cached row-item changes with stale data whenever a drag/drop happens after those edits, causing apparent data loss in the sheet until a refetch occurs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Sync local tree state from prop updates, not structure only**

This sync gate only compares a structure signature (id/path/kind), so prop updates that keep the same structure but change node content (for example renamed node labels returned from the server) are ignored and the sidebar keeps stale `localNodes`. Since rendering uses `localNodes`, users can see outdated node titles even after navigation or refreshes that provide newer `nodes` props with identical topology.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Merge tree reorder cache writes with current query state**

`onDrop` writes `nextNodes` directly into `estimateQueryKeys.areaTree(estimateId)` from `localNodes`, but row-level edits in `EstimateSheetContent` can update that same cache independently before a drag occurs. In that case, this overwrite can drop newer row-item changes from the cache until a refetch, because `nextNodes` is not derived from the latest cached tree. Build the optimistic reorder from the current cache value (or merge before writing) to avoid clobbering concurrent local edits.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refresh local tree when prop content changes without structure change**

The sync effect only compares `getEstimateTreeStructureSignature`, so prop updates that keep the same topology (e.g., renamed node titles or changed totals) are ignored and `localNodes` remains stale. Since rendering reads from `localNodes`, users can keep seeing outdated node data after a server refresh unless the structure also changes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accept server tree updates that match prior signature**

The `incomingStructure === lastAcceptedPropStructureRef.current` guard can drop legitimate server updates: after a successful local reorder, `lastAcceptedPropStructureRef` still holds the pre-drop signature, so if the backend later sends a real update whose structure matches that earlier signature (for example, another reorder returning nodes to the prior layout), this effect keeps `currentNodes` and never resyncs to props. That leaves the sidebar on stale local state until some different structure change happens.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Re-sync local tree after pending reorder finishes**

When `nodes` props change while a reorder request is in flight, this early return skips the sync entirely, and the effect will not re-run when the request later finishes because the dependency list only includes `nodes` (the ref change does not trigger re-execution). In practice, a route refresh/navigation update that arrives during save can leave `localNodes` stuck on stale optimistic state until another unrelated prop change happens.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prevent stale reorder completions from clobbering newer edits**

A reorder request captures a snapshot of `localNodes`, but while that request is in flight the UI still allows add-node actions that mutate the tree/cache. When the reorder promise resolves, this unconditional write replaces state with the server reorder payload (or rollback snapshot on error), which can drop those newer edits from the sidebar and query cache until a later refetch/navigation. This is reproducible by starting a drag-drop save, then clicking Add Group/Add Node before the save returns.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle MIME-less attachment uploads**

`POST /api/component-library/attachments` hard-rejects any file whose browser-provided `file.type` is missing or nonstandard before relying on magic-byte detection, so valid PDF/XLS/XLSX files from environments that omit MIME metadata (common with drag/drop and some browsers/OS integrations) are rejected with a 400. Because this endpoint already reads signatures (`readMagicMime`), the strict `file.type` gate causes avoidable upload failures for legitimate files.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clean up uploaded attachments on draft discard**

Attachments are uploaded to Supabase immediately in `handleAttachmentUpload`, but the discard path only calls `cleanupUploadedDraftImages`, which removes image uploads only; removed/discarded attachments are just dropped from local state and never deleted from storage. In workflows where users upload attachments and cancel/close or remove them before save, this leaks orphaned files and steadily increases storage usage.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify XLSX payload beyond ZIP magic bytes**

`readMagicMime` treats any payload beginning with `PK` as XLSX, but `PK` is only the generic ZIP signature and is shared by many non-spreadsheet files (including other Office document types). A client that sets `file.type` to XLSX can upload arbitrary ZIP-based content that passes validation and is stored as a spreadsheet attachment, which breaks the endpoint’s file-type contract and can surface unusable files to users.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match remote image protocol to Supabase URL**

The Supabase remote pattern is hardcoded to `https`, so when `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` points to a local/dev Supabase instance over `http` (the standard local setup), valid storage URLs no longer match `images.remotePatterns` and `next/image` rejects them. This breaks component thumbnails in dev/test environments even though the host/path are correct.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restrict wildcard remote image hosts**

Allowing `hostname: "**"` with `pathname: "/**"` effectively permits the image optimizer to fetch arbitrary HTTPS URLs, which turns `/_next/image` into a broad remote fetch surface and can be abused for unexpected bandwidth/cost and security exposure. Next.js recommends strict `remotePatterns`; this wildcard pattern removes that protection.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

nodes.title: Add Supabase component image uploads

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow Sharp `heif` metadata for AVIF uploads**

The handler advertises AVIF support (`ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES` and magic-byte detection both accept `image/avif`), but this validation path rejects many valid AVIF files because Sharp commonly reports AVIF input metadata as `heif`, not `avif`. In that case users get `Unsupported image encoding.` even though the file type is allowed, so AVIF uploads from common sources can fail consistently.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep storage paths to clean up replaced/cancelled uploads**

After a successful upload, the client stores only the public thumbnail URL in draft state and drops the returned storage object paths. That means if the user uploads another image, closes the modal, or the later component save fails, there is no identifier available to remove the previously uploaded objects, leaving orphaned files in the public bucket over time.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Block save while thumbnail upload is still running**

`handleThumbnailUpload` updates `draft.thumbnailPath` only after awaiting the network upload, so there is a window where the form can still be submitted with an empty/old thumbnail value. In that window, users can click Save while `imageUpload.state` is `processing`/`uploading`, creating the component without the new image and potentially leaving the just-uploaded file unreferenced when the async upload finishes later.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve support for legacy non-Supabase thumbnail hosts**

This config now allows `next/image` remote loading only from the Supabase bucket host, but the component list now renders `item.imageUrl` through `next/image`. Components created before this change could already contain arbitrary absolute URLs (the prior Add Component form accepted free-text image URL/path), so those records can now trigger `next/image` host validation errors instead of rendering thumbnails.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accept AVIF files with non-`avif` major brands**

The AVIF sniffing path only accepts files whose `ftyp` major brand is exactly `avif`, but valid AVIF files can use other major brands (for example `avis`) while still declaring AVIF compatibility in the brand list. In those cases this branch returns `null`, so the request is rejected as unsupported before Sharp runs, even though the upload is a valid AVIF image type the endpoint claims to support.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow MIME-less image uploads to reach magic-byte validation**

The handler rejects uploads when `file.type` is not in the allowlist, but browsers can legitimately provide an empty `File.type` for some files/extensions. Because this check runs before magic-byte sniffing, otherwise valid JPEG/PNG/WebP/AVIF files are rejected with a 400 even though the server already has content-based validation to determine the real format.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Persist full-size image reference or stop uploading it**

The upload API returns both `url/path` (full-size) and `thumbnailUrl/thumbnailPath`, but this modal only persists `thumbnailUrl` into `draft.thumbnailPath`, so every successful upload leaves the full-size object unreferenced and effectively orphaned from the data model. This causes guaranteed storage bloat even when the component is saved successfully, because there is no record field that can later render or clean up the full-size object.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow MIME-less files to reach server-side image sniffing**

This client-side gate rejects files when `file.type` is empty, but browsers can legitimately provide an empty MIME for valid image files, so users can be blocked before the server's magic-byte validation runs. In those environments, valid JPEG/PNG/WebP/AVIF uploads will fail immediately with a client error despite the backend already implementing content-based format checks.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed the Codex image-upload review comments in b504895. Summary:

- AVIF uploads now accept compatible ftyp brands and Sharp's heif metadata when magic-byte sniffing identifies image/avif.
- MIME-less client/server uploads now pass through to server-side magic-byte validation instead of being rejected early.
- Add Component now blocks save/close while thumbnail upload is running.
- Uploaded full-size + thumbnail object paths/URLs are persisted in component metadata so the full-size object is not orphaned after a successful save.
- Replaced/cancelled draft uploads are cleaned up through a DELETE handler that only removes objects under the current workspace/user prefix.
- Legacy external thumbnail URLs are rendered with a plain image fallback instead of broadening next/image remotePatterns beyond the Supabase bucket.

Validation run locally:
- bun run lint
- bun run validate
- git diff --check
- npx gitnexus analyze
- npx gitnexus detect-changes --repo /private/tmp/archestimator-image-clean --scope unstaged

Note: GitNexus detect-changes reports critical because the image upload route is on authenticated request flows; individual symbol impact checks for the edited Add Component and create component paths were LOW, and the pre-commit hook reported overall risk score 0.00.

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update the cost field that totals actually use**

When a line item comes from the library with `materialUnitCost` set and no `unitCost` (as in the seed data), the grid now displays that material cost in the editable Unit cost cell, but this edit path still writes the new value to `unitCost`. `calculateEstimateLineTotal` prefers `materialUnitCost ?? unitCost`, so the cell can show the edited price while the row total and live grand total continue using the old material cost, producing inconsistent estimate results for material-library rows.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Map new project rows to the default proposal section**

For projects created through this path, the working section and proposal section get different ids, but the current add-row flows only populate `sectionId` and never set `proposalSectionId`. When the user adds any line to a brand-new project and issues a proposal, `createProposalSnapshot` cannot match the line to `General Requirements`, so that summary stays at 0 and the actual amount is forced into `Unassigned Proposal Section`, making the default proposal output misleading.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude non-billable rows from section header totals**

When a line in the section is marked `excluded`, `by-others`, or `not-applicable`, the live grand total and proposal summaries skip it via `calculateEstimateTotals`, but this section header total still sums the raw line amount. In that scenario the grid can show a nonzero section total while the billable total is zero, so users see contradictory estimate totals in the same sheet.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid silently mapping new rows to the first proposal section**

In the seeded estimate, selecting the `GEN · Project-wide` working section and adding a blank/library row still assigns `proposal_section_floor_finishes`, because this helper ignores `selectedSectionId` and always returns the first displayed proposal section. That means new General Conditions work is included under Floor Finishes in the proposal preview/snapshot with no “Needs proposal mapping” warning, so users can issue misclassified section totals.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Account for grid scroll when resolving drop rows**

For estimates with more rows than the visible grid, dropping after scrolling vertically still computes the target from the pointer’s viewport position only. Since the DataEditor scroll offset is not included here, a drop over a visible lower row after scrolling maps back to the same top-of-viewport row index, inserting library items into the wrong section/line once the grid has enough rows to scroll.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid defaulting unmatched spaces to the first proposal section**

When a working section has no existing mapped rows, this fallback still silently assigns the first displayed proposal section even if the selected space does not match it. In the seeded data, if the user deletes the only `GEN · Project-wide` row and then adds another row to that space, the token match against `General Conditions` scores 0, so the new row is assigned to `Floor Finishes` instead of staying unmapped and triggering the proposal-mapping warning. Fresh evidence in this revision: the new inference only succeeds while a previously mapped row remains in the working section.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mark linked rows overridden from grid edits**

When a user edits a linked library row through the new Glide grid, this path applies the cell change directly and never runs the same `detectLinkStateAfterEdit` logic used by the table controls. For linked-clean rows, changing the item, unit, or unit cost in the primary spreadsheet leaves `linkState` as `linked-clean`, so the estimate can misrepresent overridden library pricing as still synchronized.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Constrain scope edits before saving**

When users edit the Scope column in this new production grid, the adapter accepts arbitrary text and stores it as `scopeStatus`; a typo such as `exclude` is not one of the schema enum values, so Save estimate or Issue proposal will later hit `repository.saveDatabase` validation and refuse to write the database. The existing accessible table avoids this by using a fixed select, so the grid should either make scope non-freeform or validate/remap it before applying the edit.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Track the Next ambient declarations**

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mark grid edits as library overrides**

When a library-backed row is edited through the primary Glide grid, this path mutates fields like name/unit/cost but never transitions `linkState` to `linked-overridden` the way the table controls do via `detectLinkStateAfterEdit`. A user can therefore change a linked library rate in the production grid and still see/export the row as `linked-clean`, masking that the estimate no longer matches the library source.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp grid numeric edits to nonnegative values**

The Glide edit path accepts any finite number, so entering a negative quantity, unit cost, or waste percent in the grid updates the estimate even though the schema requires those fields to be nonnegative and the accessible inputs clamp them at zero. After such an edit, totals can go negative and Save/Issue will fail schema validation when persisting the local database.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Format proposal history dates deterministically**

When a project has issued proposals, this client component is still pre-rendered on the server, and `toLocaleDateString()` uses the host defaults. A UTC server and a browser in another timezone/locale can render different text for the same `issuedAt` value, causing hydration mismatches and, for timestamps near midnight UTC, showing the wrong proposal date in history. Use an explicit locale/timeZone or precomputed display date instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep ADRs in canonical .ai locations**

This adds a durable decision under a new `.ai/05_decisions` folder, but the project instructions in `AGENTS.md` route agents through the canonical `.ai` map, where `05` is reserved for logs and durable decisions belong in `.ai/10_state/decisions.md` or a relevant spec. Keeping the detailed ADR here creates a second decision silo that future agents following the documented map are likely to miss; move it into a canonical folder or update the map before adding this location.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pass the edited revision to the server action**

When the user edits the sheet or clicks “Duplicate draft locally”, this button still calls `duplicateRevisionAction` with only `estimate.id`; the server then reloads the old estimate from `runtime.json` and duplicates that stale copy, so unsaved row/rate changes are dropped, and after a local duplicate the generated `estimate_rev_...` id is not in the repository and the action throws `Estimate not found`. Persist the current `estimate` payload (or make the server-side duplicate happen before creating the local revision) so the “Save as persisted revision” flow does not lose or reject the visible draft.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Number proposal snapshots per project**

In a workspace with proposals on multiple projects, this uses the global `database.proposalSnapshots.length`, so the first proposal issued for a second project can be labeled `Initial Proposal 2` (or higher) even though that project has no prior proposal history. Since the label is stored in the immutable snapshot and shown in proposal history/print output, count existing snapshots for the same project or estimate before assigning the next proposal number.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve library waste when pricing inserted rows**

When a library item defines `defaultWastePercent` (the demo tile does with 10%), this insertion path only copies the unit costs, and the resulting estimate row has no waste value for `calculateEstimateTotals` to pass into `calculateEstimateLineTotal`. Any library material that relies on waste is therefore priced too low after insertion or reset; for example, 25 sqm of the demo tile should use 27.5 sqm before material/labor subtotals.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Format totals with the workspace currency**

The local database carries `workspace.defaultCurrency`, but all totals and proposal amounts are formatted through this module-level formatter hard-coded to PHP. Any workspace or seed changed to another currency will still show peso amounts throughout the estimate sheet and proposal preview, corrupting the visible financial output even though the data model says the currency is configurable.
